contextCompiler.purpose: Compile minimum sufficient, evidence-linked context for one task without replacing HEAD authority.
contextCompiler.authority: Materialized context is derived and rebuildable; canonical sources and user-owned decisions remain authoritative.
contextCompiler.failurePolicy: Fail closed on canon drift; harness adapters may fail open to normal agent operation when compilation is unavailable.

executionLineage.purpose: Connect whole-plan authority, bounded execution, evidence-linked results, and HEAD review without relying on provider conversation state.
executionLineage.identity: Artifacts use content-derived identifiers, digest verification, and typed parent relationships.
executionLineage.status: Contract-bound Runs, evidence-linked Result Packets, deterministic Fresh HEAD review projections, ReviewDecision-linked plan generations, and authority-free knowledge proposals are active; provider runtime hydration and authorized promotion are deferred.

productModel.purpose: Preserve user-owned product intent independently from repository layout and project it into rebuildable temporal evidence.
productModel.authority: The source document is mutable user-owned project canon. Graph nodes, graph edges, ContextCapsule ProductContext, and documents are derived projections and cannot mutate or promote canon.
productModel.status: Strict schema validation, stable logical keys, immutable content-derived revisions, Git-independent GraphSnapshot projection, bounded Context Compiler selection, and explicit onboarding ReviewDecision promotion are active; product-to-code mappings and general relationship promotion remain deferred.

onboarding.purpose: Bootstrap a project-scoped HEAD Session and Product Canon without silently turning observed code, documentation, model inference, or storage capability into authority.
onboarding.authority: Candidates and GraphSnapshots remain non-authoritative. Only an explicit ReviewDecision with decisionScope product-canon-bootstrap may create a new Product Canon revision.
onboarding.storage: Local JSON is complete by default. GraphDB endpoint, database, and secret-reference names may be recorded as pending operational configuration; credential values are rejected and the remote adapter is not claimed active.
onboarding.status: Project-scoped Session records, deterministic legacy migration, evidence-linked bounded candidate inference, stale-source rejection, batch review, immutable decision receipts, Product Canon revision history, and post-promotion GraphSnapshot verification are active.

computeAdapter.purpose: Delegate deterministic heavy computation without changing semantic identity or transferring authority from the JavaScript control plane.
computeAdapter.identity: Canonical operation, input digest, semantic producer, and normalized limits determine the request; canonical complete output determines the result digest. Backend diagnostics are excluded.
computeAdapter.authority: Computation only with no instruction, promotion, control, project-mutation, or canon-mutation authority.
computeAdapter.status: Strict request/response validation, resource limits, timeout/cancellation, structured errors, authority-escalation rejection, verified Go stdio transport, platform manifest integrity checks, bounded exact-child lifecycle, disclosed JavaScript fallback, and health-response conformance are active. A Go repository.scan.v1 candidate is complete-response conformant, but production manifests retain the JavaScript path because measured benefit is not yet material across repository sizes.

worldModel.purpose: Materialize rebuildable repository file, symbol, dependency, import, and call evidence for task-specific compilation.
worldModel.store: replaceable-rebuildable-materialized-view via a versioned WorldModelStoreAdapter; local-json is the active adapter
worldModel.authority: Derived evidence only; project canon and user-owned decisions remain authoritative.
worldModel.coverage: Supported text files, heuristic symbols/dependencies, evidence-linked file/symbol/import/call graph, user-owned Product Model canon, a Git-independent temporal Product/File/Symbol/Test revision GraphSnapshot, all reachable Git commit-message decision evidence, current Git refs, canonical HEAD lifecycle state, point-in-time host-exported external runtime observations, and bounded product/semantic/temporal/history/runtime traversal are active; ChangeSet and product-to-code projection, AST-accurate analysis, structured Git decision inference, live runtime probing/control, document projections, and the optional GraphDB adapter are deferred.

temporalProvenance.purpose: Connect stable product and repository entities to immutable content-derived revisions and explicit multiple-parent ancestry without requiring Git or GraphDB.
temporalProvenance.identity: Logical identities exclude line locations, Git objects, GraphDB records, provider sessions, and document page IDs; revisions and graph/query/result artifacts are digest-verifiable.
temporalProvenance.authority: Rebuildable derived evidence only with no instruction, promotion, canonical, or unique authority.
temporalProvenance.status: Product Canon projection, zero-or-more SourceSnapshot and Revision parents, and deterministic bounded traversal are active; automatic merge, conflict resolution, inferred candidate promotion, product-to-code mappings, and remote GraphProjectionAdapter backends are deferred.

roles.head: Owns whole-outcome understanding, strategy, integration, and completion judgment.
roles.developer: Owns one bounded, independently consumable implementation result.
roles.coder: Implements a fully decided Run contract without changing observable behavior.
roles.reviewer: Evaluates consequential decisions before implementation without choosing the final direction.

invariants: The user retains material product, policy, architecture, cost, workflow, and external-action authority.
Canonical project state outranks conversation summaries and transient logs.
A project identifier maps to one canonical project root.
Managed files are never overwritten after user modification.
Runtime-specific sessions remain distinct from HEAD session and Run identifiers.
